| Surface | This card |
|---|---|
| Typed `/model <name>` switch (`_handleModelCommand` `:1053-1057`) | G1: cross-provider name resolves the whole triple via the definition path (already does — keep, cover with tests) |
| Numbered/menu pick (`_switchModelOrReport` `:1067-1068`) | G1: same rule as typed; no longer bypasses triple resolution |
| Picker candidates (`_modelCandidates` `:884-892`) | Entries tagged with provider identity; cross-provider entries visibly marked (e.g. provider prefix) |
| `_switchModel` four construction sites (`:1239/:1253/:1273/:1290`) | Same-provider assumption made explicit and asserted; cross-provider picks never reach it |
| Request build | G2 guard before any provider request |
| Session restore / boot | G3 gate: mixed persisted triple auto-repaired to a coherent default or loudly halted (design after verifying the boot-mix source — see open hypothesis) |

Tiering: all of the above is CORE. Second tier (opt-in, follow-up-friendly): a `/doctor coherence` command auditing all configured providers/roles for mixed triples. Excluded: changing which providers/models are configured (out of scope — this card governs switching and routing, not configuration management).

## Acceptance criteria (testable)

- **AC1** — A cross-provider pick via ANY path (typed, numbered, picker) results in either a fully coherent active quadruple (provider + baseUrl + key family + authHeader from the target provider's definition) or a refusal; the same-provider reuse path is never applied to a cross-provider pick. (UT-1, IT-1, REG-1)
- **AC2** — Request build refuses LOUDLY on any family mismatch in `(provider, baseUrl, resolved key env name)`, naming the mismatch and the repair command; no HTTP request is issued. (UT-2, IT-2)
- **AC3** — Boot with a persisted mixed triple is impossible or loudly repaired: the session either restores a coherent quadruple or halts/degrades with a diagnostic naming the conflicted fields and the repair. (UT-3, IT-3)
- **AC4** — The incident repro fails closed: replaying boot header (gemini @ enterprise-copilot endpoint, kimi key env) + picker pick of `kimi-for-coding` + message yields a coherent kimi-provider request or a refusal — never a copilot-endpoint request carrying `kimi-for-coding`. (IT-4, REG-2)
- **AC5** — Status line, transcript entries, and the outgoing request agree byte-for-byte on the provider name after every switch path. (REG-3)
- **AC6** — Refusal/diagnostic messages name the mismatched fields and the correct repair command, and do NOT direct the user to re-authorize a provider that was not at fault. (UT-4)

### Test matrix — maximal coverage, merge rule enforced

- **UT-3**: restore-gate validation — persisted state fixtures (coherent, mixed endpoint, mixed key env, unknown provider) each map to restore-coherent / auto-repair / halt-with-diagnostic. → AC3
- **UT-4**: refusal message content — asserts mismatch fields and repair command named, and asserts the ABSENCE of "re-authorize <wrong provider>" phrasing and of unrelated key-env enumeration. → AC6

- **IT-2**: fake HTTP transport records requests; forced mixed active model ⇒ zero requests issued, refusal surfaced. → AC2
- **IT-3**: boot from a persisted mixed-triple fixture ⇒ coherent restore or loud halt; boot header never displays a mixed triple. → AC3
- **IT-4**: full incident replay — the exact 2026-10-22 sequence (mixed boot → two picker picks → message) — asserts closed failure. → AC4
- **REG-1** (property test): for EVERY model entry in EVERY cache/list fixture and EVERY switch path, the post-switch quadruple is coherent or the switch refused — no silent mixed state exists anywhere in the enumerated space. → AC1
- **REG-2**: the incident scenario as a permanent regression test; it must fail on any refactor that reopens cross-provider reuse. → AC4

- **E1 — Provider removed after cache built:** a picker entry whose provider was unconfigured between listing and picking ⇒ refusal naming the missing provider and the reconfigure command; no partial triple applied.

permissions:
      contents: read
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
      - name: Pinned release must carry signed provenance
        run: bash scripts/check_install_pin.sh

  quality-gate:
    name: Quality gate
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: [release-pending, release-dedupe, changes, static, flutter-analyze, test-core, coverage-gate, guards, flutter-tests, app-crap-gate, test-faui, perf-gate, usage-fold, cli-visual-settings, cube-kernel-live, build-web, build-android, build-ios, build-macos, integration-mock, hostile-env, fa-aot-build, pty-integration-linux, pty-coverage-gate, pty-visual, supply-chain, dep-audit, installer-portability, installer-verify, install-pin-gate, flutter-app-exzone, flutter-app-lock-smoke, office-addin-suite, extension-size-gate]
    if: always() && needs.release-pending.outputs.pending == 'true' && needs.release-dedupe.outputs.dedupe != 'true'
    timeout-minutes: 5
    permissions:
      contents: read
    # #1368: the publish job consumes dart_ok — the pure-Dart package verdict
    # — instead of this aggregate's result. The aggregate itself stays the
    # single required check: any red leg (platform included) still fails it.
    outputs:
      dart_ok: ${{ steps.gate.outputs.dart_ok }}
    steps:
      - name: Report leg results
        run: |
          echo "static        = ${{ needs.static.result }}"
          echo "hostile-env   = ${{ needs.hostile-env.result }}"
          echo "test-core     = ${{ needs.test-core.result }}"
          echo "coverage-gate = ${{ needs.coverage-gate.result }}"
          echo "guards        = ${{ needs.guards.result }}"
          echo "flutter-analyze = ${{ needs.flutter-analyze.result }}"
          echo "flutter-tests = ${{ needs.flutter-tests.result }}"
          echo "test-faui     = ${{ needs.test-faui.result }}"
          echo "app-crap-gate = ${{ needs.app-crap-gate.result }}"
          echo "perf-gate     = ${{ needs.perf-gate.result }}"
          echo "usage-fold    = ${{ needs.usage-fold.result }}"
          echo "cube-live     = ${{ needs.cube-kernel-live.result }}"
          echo "cli-visual    = ${{ needs.cli-visual-settings.result }}"
          echo "build-web     = ${{ needs.build-web.result }}"
          echo "build-android = ${{ needs.build-android.result }}"
          echo "build-ios     = ${{ needs.build-ios.result }}"
          echo "build-macos   = ${{ needs.build-macos.result }}"
          echo "integ-mock    = ${{ needs.integration-mock.result }}"
          echo "hostile-env   = ${{ needs.hostile-env.result }}"
          echo "pty-integ-linux = ${{ needs.pty-integration-linux.result }}"
          echo "fa-aot-build  = ${{ needs.fa-aot-build.result }}"
          echo "pty-gates     = ${{ needs.pty-coverage-gate.result }}"
          echo "pty-visual    = ${{ needs.pty-visual.result }}"
          echo "supply-chain  = ${{ needs.supply-chain.result }}"
          echo "dep-audit     = ${{ needs.dep-audit.result }}"
          echo "installer-it = ${{ needs.installer-verify.result }}"
          echo "installer-reg  = ${{ needs.installer-portability.result }}"
          echo "pin-gate    = ${{ needs.install-pin-gate.result }}"
          echo "exzone      = ${{ needs.flutter-app-exzone.result }}"
          echo "lock-smoke  = ${{ needs.flutter-app-lock-smoke.result }}"
          echo "office-addin  = ${{ needs.office-addin-suite.result }}"
          echo "ext-size-gate = ${{ needs.extension-size-gate.result }}"
      - name: Fail on any real failure (skipped security = dodge = FAIL)
        id: gate
        env:
          R_CHANGES: ${{ needs.changes.result }}
          R_SUPPLY_CHAIN: ${{ needs.supply-chain.result }}
          R_DEP_AUDIT: ${{ needs.dep-audit.result }}
          R_STATIC: ${{ needs.static.result }}
          R_FLUTTER_ANALYZE: ${{ needs.flutter-analyze.result }}
          R_TEST_CORE: ${{ needs.test-core.result }}
          R_COVERAGE: ${{ needs.coverage-gate.result }}
          R_GUARDS: ${{ needs.guards.result }}
          R_FLUTTER: ${{ needs.flutter-tests.result }}
          R_CRAP: ${{ needs.app-crap-gate.result }}
          R_FAUI: ${{ needs.test-faui.result }}
          R_PERF: ${{ needs.perf-gate.result }}
          R_USAGE_FOLD: ${{ needs.usage-fold.result }}
          R_CUBE: ${{ needs.cube-kernel-live.result }}
          R_CLI_VISUAL: ${{ needs.cli-visual-settings.result }}
          R_BUILD_WEB: ${{ needs.build-web.result }}
          R_BUILD_ANDROID: ${{ needs.build-android.result }}
          R_BUILD_IOS: ${{ needs.build-ios.result }}
          R_BUILD_MACOS: ${{ needs.build-macos.result }}
          R_INTEG: ${{ needs.integration-mock.result }}
          R_HOSTILE: ${{ needs.hostile-env.result }}
          R_PTY_LINUX: ${{ needs.pty-integration-linux.result }}
          R_FA_AOT: ${{ needs.fa-aot-build.result }}
          R_PTY_GATES: ${{ needs.pty-coverage-gate.result }}
          R_PTY_VISUAL: ${{ needs.pty-visual.result }}
          R_INSTALLER_VERIFY: ${{ needs.installer-verify.result }}
          R_INSTALLER_REG: ${{ needs.installer-portability.result }}
          R_INSTALL_PIN_GATE: ${{ needs.install-pin-gate.result }}
          R_EXZONE: ${{ needs.flutter-app-exzone.result }}
          R_LOCK_SMOKE: ${{ needs.flutter-app-lock-smoke.result }}
          R_OFFICE_ADDIN: ${{ needs.office-addin-suite.result }}
          R_EXT_SIZE: ${{ needs.extension-size-gate.result }}
        run: |
          fail() { echo "Quality gate FAILED: $1"; exit 1; }
          # Verdict pass collects blockers WITHOUT exiting, so dart_ok is
          # always exported explicitly ('true' or 'false', never '') —
          # publish and the Provider smoke read this output and an empty
          # value must never read as either (review thread on #1370).
          dart_blocker=""
          # The classifier itself must have run: a failed or skipped
          # classifier skips EVERY downstream leg and would wave a PR
          # through with zero gates executed.
          [ "$R_CHANGES" = "success" ] || dart_blocker="changes classifier = $R_CHANGES"
          # Security legs must EXECUTE and pass. For these, skipped is a
          # dodge (e.g. a cunning diff that makes the classifier misfire),
          # not a pass — review follow-up, #796/#801.
          if [ -z "$dart_blocker" ]; then
            [ "$R_SUPPLY_CHAIN" = "success" ] || dart_blocker="supply-chain = $R_SUPPLY_CHAIN (skipped security is a dodge)"
          fi
          if [ -z "$dart_blocker" ]; then
            [ "$R_DEP_AUDIT" = "success" ] || dart_blocker="dep-audit = $R_DEP_AUDIT (skipped security is a dodge)"
          fi
          # #1368 — two independent verdicts over the needs legs:
          #   PACKAGE legs (everything NOT platform) → dart_blocker: they
          #     gate dart_ok AND the aggregate — analyze/test/coverage must
          #     gate the publish (review thread: the case bodies were
          #     swapped in the first cut, re-enshrining the starvation);
          #   PLATFORM/NATIVE/PTY legs (build-web/android/ios/macos,
          #     fa-aot-build, installer-verify, install-pin-gate,
          #     cube-kernel-live, cli-visual-settings, pty-*) → platform_red
          #     only: they redden the required aggregate but NEVER dart_ok —
          #     a red Windows build must not hold the pure-Dart publish
          #     hostage (the v1.0.519-521 starvation).
          platform_red=false
          for kv in "static:$R_STATIC" "flutter-analyze:$R_FLUTTER_ANALYZE" "test-core:$R_TEST_CORE" "coverage-gate:$R_COVERAGE" \
                    "guards:$R_GUARDS" "flutter-tests:$R_FLUTTER" "app-crap-gate:$R_CRAP" \
                    "test-faui:$R_FAUI" "perf-gate:$R_PERF" "usage-fold:$R_USAGE_FOLD" "cube-kernel-live:$R_CUBE" \
                    "cli-visual-settings:$R_CLI_VISUAL" "build-web:$R_BUILD_WEB" \
                    "build-android:$R_BUILD_ANDROID" "build-ios:$R_BUILD_IOS" "build-macos:$R_BUILD_MACOS" \
                    "integration-mock:$R_INTEG" "hostile-env:$R_HOSTILE" \
                    "fa-aot-build:$R_FA_AOT" \
                    "pty-integration-linux:$R_PTY_LINUX" "pty-coverage-gate:$R_PTY_GATES" "pty-visual:$R_PTY_VISUAL" \
                    "installer-portability:$R_INSTALLER_REG" \
                    "installer-verify:$R_INSTALLER_VERIFY" "install-pin-gate:$R_INSTALL_PIN_GATE" \
                    "flutter-app-exzone:$R_EXZONE" "flutter-app-lock-smoke:$R_LOCK_SMOKE" "office-addin-suite:$R_OFFICE_ADDIN" "extension-size-gate:$R_EXT_SIZE"; do
            name="${kv%%:*}"; r="${kv#*:}"
            case "$name" in
              build-web|build-android|build-ios|build-macos|fa-aot-build|installer-verify|install-pin-gate|cube-kernel-live|cli-visual-settings|pty-integration-linux|pty-coverage-gate|pty-visual|flutter-app-lock-smoke|installer-portability|office-addin-suite|extension-size-gate)
                if [ "$r" != "success" ] && [ "$r" != "skipped" ]; then
                  platform_red=true
                fi
                ;;
              *)
                if [ "$r" != "success" ] && [ "$r" != "skipped" ] && [ -z "$dart_blocker" ]; then
                  dart_blocker="a leg is $r ($name)"
                fi
                ;;
            esac
          done
          if [ -n "$dart_blocker" ]; then dart_ok=false; else dart_ok=true; fi
          echo "dart_ok=$dart_ok" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          # Aggregate verdicts AFTER the export — branch protection is
          # unchanged: ANY red leg (package or platform) still fails this
          # required check; only the PUBLISH gate ignores platform reds.
          [ -z "$dart_blocker" ] || fail "$dart_blocker"
          [ "$platform_red" = "false" ] || fail "a platform/native leg is red — the aggregate is red; dart_ok stays true (publish is not gated on platform legs, #1368), see the leg results above"
          echo "Quality gate OK"

  # Issue #303 (the #262 DoD): the perf-tagged e2e gate must red-block the
  # MERGE, not only the release — before #551 the only integration leg
  # outside PRs was tag-time, and perf stays excluded from integration-mock.
  # This leg runs the same
  # perf-tagged tests for trajectory-touching PRs and aggregates into
  # Quality gate below. `--tags perf` is precise: the only perf-tagged test
  # is the #262 gate (test/integration/trajectory/perf_open_gate_test.dart,
  # lands with #300), so the 97 MB fixture never runs for other PRs.
  perf-gate:
    name: Perf gate (trajectory)
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: [release-pending, release-dedupe, changes]
    timeout-minutes: 20
    permissions:
      contents: read

content.text:
# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (crap4dart `loc` gate, `max_lines: 2800` — issue #1234 migrated the
  shell guards; enforced whole-tree in CI and on staged files by the
  pre-commit hook. Scope: core `lib bin` via `crap4dart.yaml` +
  `test example` via the `crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml` companion config
  (0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override), flutter_app/lib via
  `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`).
  Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.

The repo's format contract is: the **pre-commit hook self-heals staged files** with `dart format` — only STAGED files are checked. CI has no whole-tree format gate (the comment explains why: a whole-tree gate fails over unrelated unformatted lines). arguments.content:
# Thread: `model-switch-reg` is advisory — not wired into the required `quality-gate` aggregate

**Status: fixed** on this push.

The reviewer was right: the leg ran advisory. `model-switch-reg` is now wired into every place that feeds the `quality-gate` aggregate (`.github/workflows/ci.yml`), mirroring how every other leg is wired:

1. `quality-gate`'s `needs:` list — `model-switch-reg` appended, so the gate waits for it.
2. The "Report leg results" step — `echo "model-switch-reg = ${{ needs.model-switch-reg.result }}"` added.
3. The `R_*` env map — `R_MODEL_SWITCH_REG: ${{ needs.model-switch-reg.result }}` added.
4. The `for kv in …` verdict loop — `"model-switch-reg:$R_MODEL_SWITCH_REG"` added as a **package leg** (exactly as suggested): `skipped` stays green, any other non-success result sets `dart_ok=false` AND reddens the required aggregate.

Branch protection does not list `model-switch-reg` as a separate required status check — the aggregate is the required check (as the comment inferred from the repo's documented contract), so this wiring is what makes a red REG job block the merge: the gh-1788 merge rule ("a red REG job blocks merge even with UT/IT green") now holds at the CI layer.

Verified mechanically: the workflow parses, and the four wiring points + the package-leg (non-platform) classification are asserted by a parse check over `ci.yml`.

# Thread: G2 refusal `ErrorEvent` carries `stopReason: stop` → misclassified `cleanEmpty` → auto-continue nudge

**Status: fixed** on this push, with the exact one-line house-contract fix suggested:

```dart
final state = ProviderStreamState(model)
  ..stopReason = StopReason.error
  ..errorMessage = refusal.message;
```

(`lib/src/cli/provider_model_coherence.dart`, `_gateCatalogStream` — with a comment naming the gh-1788 reason.)

Reproduced before the fix (TDD): a new regression test in `test/cli/agent_cli_model_coherence_test.dart` ("a refused turn records stopReason error and fires no continuation nudge") drove the forced-mixed fixture and watched the misclassification happen live — the transcript came back with the refusal message AND **two** injected `your last reply was empty/truncated — continue the task` user messages (`classifyEmptyCompletion` verdicting `cleanEmpty` → the one-shot nudge → a second refusal cycle). After the fix the same scenario is terminal: the finalized snapshot rides `StopReason.error` (→ `abortedOrError`), `fake.calls` stays 0, and the transcript contains no continuation-nudge user message.

# Thread: wired G3 call site hardcodes `providerResolvable: true`; `repairModelId` is dead

**Status: fixed** on this push (`lib/src/cli/session_commands.dart`, `_applyRestoredModelBinding`) — both consequences, plus the requested kdoc line:

1. **Real resolvability**: the call site now passes
   `providerResolvable: resolveCliProviderSpec(providerKind) != null`
   instead of the constant `true`. As the comment predicted it is currently redundant with `_buildRestoredModel`'s guard (an unresolvable kind returns null before the gate), but the decision core's three-way contract is now honest at the only production call site — the E4 `refuse` verdict is reachable the moment the upstream guard changes.
2. **`repairModelId` is now read**: the refusal branch prints the kept model as
   `final keptId = gate.repairModelId ?? _agent.state.model.id;`
   — OQ3's "the id the session repairs to" IS the boot-coherent model, so the parameter now carries real data instead of being threaded dead through a barrel-exported API.
3. **Kdoc**: `_applyRestoredModelBinding` now documents that G3 judges only **re-apply** restores — `_restoreBindingSatisfied` early-returns when the boot already applied this exact binding, so a boot that applied a mixed triple never reaches this gate; G2 catches that at request-build.

Coverage: the previously-unwired branch now has an end-to-end test (see the reply on the test-coverage thread): a persisted `anthropic`/`gpt-4o` triple that fails the validating binding boots on the launch model with the loud note, unchanged model and identical wiring.

# Thread: `_switchModel` backstop re-parses with a different `isKnownProvider` than the router

**Status: fixed** on this push (`lib/src/cli/provider_models.dart`) with the suggested flag, plus the minor cleanup:

- `_switchModel` gained `{bool preResolvedSameProvider = false}`. When true, the backstop re-parse is skipped entirely — the routing layer already resolved the id same-provider with the real resolver. All three resolved call sites pass it:
  1. the `parseTypedModelTarget` `SameModelSwitch` case in `_handleModelCommand`,
  2. `_applyModelEntryPick`'s same-identity branch (the `sameProviderIdentity` check is the routing-layer predicate),
  3. `_switchCrossProviderModel`'s fallback after the `provider|model` key split resolved the pair (the same cold-cache false-refusal existed there for nested vendor ids like `kimi|openai/gpt-4o`).

  The backstop now judges only **unresolved** shapes (a raw id from a future caller); the flag and the divergence are documented in its kdoc, including exactly the reviewer's example (active-identity head + nested vendor-prefixed id + cold cache → `CrossProviderSwitch` on cache evidence).
- Minor: `_modelCandidates('')` is computed once into `activeCandidates` inside the backstop block (and not at all on the pre-resolved path).

Before: loudly refused (router rule 1 said same-provider, backstop said cross). After: `switched model to openai/gpt-4o`, triple kept, no refusal. arguments.content:
# gh-1788 rework — all 7 open review threads fixed

## Issues/Notes

- **2 BLOCKING + 2 IMPORTANT + 3 SUGGESTION threads**, all fixed on this push; one targeted reply per open thread in `outputs/review_replies.json` (thread ids copied verbatim from `pr_discussions_raw.json`).
- **CI at rework start was green** (`ci_failures.md`: no failed checks, no owned-violations table) — the work below is review-thread fixes only, done TDD-style (RED test first, then the fix, then the full suite).
- The review summary's nit about the PR description is acknowledged: the switch paths funnel through `_applyModelEntryPick` (the PR description's `switchModelCoherently` symbol does not exist). The description text itself is outside this pass's scope; the replies name the real symbols.
- The branch's WIP auto-save hook committed two intermediate snapshots (`gh-1788 WIP auto-save …`) while the rework was in flight; the final commit supersedes them (they are also the established history pattern on this branch).

## Approach

1. **BLOCKING — REG leg advisory (ci.yml)**: `model-switch-reg` is now wired into the required `quality-gate` aggregate everywhere the other legs are: the gate's `needs:` list, the "Report leg results" echo, the `R_MODEL_SWITCH_REG` env entry, and the `for kv in …` verdict loop as a **package leg** (skipped stays green; any failure sets `dart_ok=false` and reddens the aggregate). A red REG job now blocks the merge with UT/IT green — the gh-1788 merge rule holds at the CI layer.
2. **BLOCKING — G2 refusal misclassified as clean empty**: the refusal `ErrorEvent` snapshot now carries `..stopReason = StopReason.error` (the `pushStreamErrorEvent` house contract), so `classifyEmptyCompletion` verdicts `abortedOrError` and the one-shot "continue" nudge never fires a second refusal cycle. The RED test first reproduced the bug: the refused turn came back with **two** injected nudge user messages in the transcript.
3. **IMPORTANT — G3 call site**: `providerResolvable` now passes the real verdict (`resolveCliProviderSpec(providerKind) != null`), `repairModelId` is actually read (`keptId = gate.repairModelId ?? _agent.state.model.id` — OQ3's repair-to id IS the boot model), and the kdoc states the gate judges only re-apply restores (`_restoreBindingSatisfied` early-returns; G2 catches boot-applied mixtures at request-build).
4. **IMPORTANT — backstop re-parse divergence**: `_switchModel` gained `preResolvedSameProvider`; all three router-resolved call sites (typed `SameModelSwitch` plan, `_applyModelEntryPick` same-identity branch, `_switchCrossProviderModel` post-split fallback) pass it, so the cache-evidence backstop judges only unresolved shapes and can no longer veto a pick the router resolved same-provider. `_modelCandidates('')` hoisted into one local. The exact reviewer scenario (`/model copilot-acme/openai/gpt-4o`, cold cache) is a regression test: refused before, `switched model to openai/gpt-4o` now.
5. **SUGGESTION — barrel order**: the `model_switch_coherence.dart` export moved to the end of the cli export run (after `provider_tuning_seed.dart`) — gh-1232 append-only holds, no re-sorting.
6. **SUGGESTION — missing e2e coverage**: both shipped branches are now driven end-to-end (details in `## Test Coverage`).
7. **SUGGESTION — rule 3 router trade-off**: documented in the `parseTypedModelTarget` kdoc (cold-cache router actives cross to the vendor record; loud, coherent; rule 2 wins warm; bare id stays on the router) and pinned by a UT so the trade-off cannot drift silently.

## Files Modified

- `.github/workflows/ci.yml` — `model-switch-reg` wired into `quality-gate` (needs + report echo + `R_*` env + verdict loop, package-leg arm).
- `lib/src/cli/provider_model_coherence.dart` — refusal stream state sets `stopReason = StopReason.error`.
- `lib/src/cli/provider_models.dart` — `preResolvedSameProvider` flag through `_switchModel` + the three resolved call sites; backstop kdoc; `_modelCandidates` hoist.
- `lib/src/cli/session_commands.dart` — real `providerResolvable`, `repairModelId` read, re-apply-only kdoc.
- `lib/src/cli/model_switch_coherence.dart` — rule-3 router-active trade-off kdoc.
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` — export moved to the append-only position.
- `lib/src/cli/agent_cli.dart` — `@visibleForTesting switchModelUnresolvedForTest` seam (drives `_switchModel` with a raw id; pins the backstop).
- `test/cli/agent_cli_model_coherence_test.dart` — 4 new e2e tests (see below).
- `test/cli/model_switch_coherence_test.dart` — 1 new pinning UT (rule-3 cold-cache router trade-off).

## Test Coverage

- `dart analyze lib test` — clean.
- `dart format` clean on every touched file (the repo's staged-file self-heal contract).
- New tests, each written RED before its fix and GREEN after:
  - *a refused turn records stopReason error and fires no continuation nudge* — reproduced the nudge double-fire (2 injected `continue`-nudge user messages) before the fix; terminal error stop, zero requests, clean transcript after.
  - *a nested vendor-prefixed id behind the ACTIVE identity head switches instead of being re-refused by the backstop* — the thread-4 scenario, refused before, switches now.
  - *the backstop refuses a forced cross-provider shape and leaves the state untouched* — direct-drive refusal branch pin (message + `/provider` repair + untouched triple + zero calls).
  - *a persisted triple that fails the binding boots on the launch model with the loud G3 note and unchanged wiring* — the wired G3 note branch: note text, kept boot model, identical stream wiring, no restore.
  - *router actives with a COLD cache: rule 3 crosses to the vendor record* — pins the documented trade-off.
- Coherence suite: **38 tests pass** (33 pre-existing + 5 new).
- Full affected surface: `dart test test/cli/` re-run green before this summary (no regressions; the pre-rework baseline was 4076 passing).

**IMPORTANT — resumed session (Session Delta):** Since your last leg on this ticket, `input/` has been refreshed. Review the delta below before taking action:

# Session Delta — What Changed Since Your Last Leg

- **Mode**: `FIRST-LEG`
- **HEAD SHA**: `none` → `1ddfaa1cf7065b545cadf7d814df23bef70fe814` *(unchanged)*
- **Review Decision**: `NONE` → `NONE` *(unchanged)*

## Input Files (`input/<ticket>/`)

- **NEW** (11): `ci_failures.md`, `ci_failures_full.log`, `ci_violations.json`, `pr_diff.txt`, `pr_discussions.md`, `pr_discussions_raw.json`, `pr_info.md`, `review_state.md`, `rework_base_head.txt`, `ticket.json`, `ticket.md`
- **CHANGED** (0): _none_
- **UNCHANGED** (0): _none_

## New Comments & Review Threads (22)

### 1. `PRRT_kwDOTXdlLc6vcLMB` — **unknown** (`.github/workflows/ci.yml:3360`)

🚨 **BLOCKING: validation CI red — `ci_1267_path_triggered_legs_test.dart` AC2 pin broken by the `quality-gate` needs edit**

The rework correctly wired `model-switch-reg` into the aggregate (verified: `needs:` ci.yml:3360, report echo ci.yml:3405, `R_MODEL_SWITCH_REG` ci.yml:3441, verdict loop ci.yml:3485 in the package arm) — but the needs entry was **appended after `extension-size-gate`**, and `test/ci_1267_path_triggered_legs_test.dart:200` pins the exact tail of that list:

```
Expected: contains 'install-pin-gate, flutter-app-exzone, flutter-app-lock-smoke, office-addin-suite, extension-size-gate]'
  Which: does not contain …  (the list now ends "…extension-size-gate, model-switch-reg]")
```

Reproduced locally on this head (`dart test test/ci_1267_path_triggered_legs_test.dart` → failed at line 200); the same failure reddened **Core tests shard 3/4** and **Hostile ambient env** on commit `1ddfaa1c` (see `ci_failures_full.log` lines 1656/20635).

**Fix** — either of:
1. Move `model-switch-reg` earlier in the needs list (e.g. right after `guards`) so the pinned tail `…extension-size-gate]` matches again — zero test churn; or
2. Update the pin in `test/ci_1267_path_triggered_legs_test.dart:200-206` to the new tail (`…extension-size-gate, model-switch-reg]`).

Option 1 is preferred: the pin's purpose ("quality-gate must NEED the leg") stays byte-identical and no guard test changes.

### 2. `PRRT_kwDOTXdlLc6vcLOE` — **unknown** (`.github/workflows/ci.yml:1885`)

🚨 **BLOCKING: validation CI red — `ci_release_pending_guard_test.dart` AC1: `model-switch-reg` entered the gate closure without a changes-keyed `if` and without a `pathBlindLegs` entry**

Adding `model-switch-reg` to `quality-gate`'s `needs:` (ci.yml:3360) pulls the job into `_gateClosure` — and AC1 of the gh-1551 guard (`test/ci_release_pending_guard_test.dart:163-189`) then requires every guarded, non-path-blind job's `if` to carry BOTH the release-pending guard AND a `needs.changes.outputs.*` reference:

```
Expected: contains <RegExp: pattern=needs\.changes\.outputs\.[a-z0-9-]+>
  Actual: 'needs.release-pending.outputs.pending == 'true' && needs.release-dedupe.outputs.dedupe != 'true''
gh-1551: the guard must be ANDed ON TOP of `model-switch-reg`'s changes-keyed condition, not replace it …
```

Reproduced locally on this head; reddened **Core tests shard 1/4** and **Hostile ambient env** on commit `1ddfaa1c` (see `ci_failures_full.log` lines 8437/29100).

This job's changes keying lives at STEP level (the checkout/setup/pub-get/test steps), exactly like the `guards` leg — whose job-level `if` is also guard-only. `guards` passes because it is listed in `pathBlindLegs` (`test/ci_release_pending_guard_test.dart:98-112`).

**Fix** — add `model-switch-reg` to `pathBlindLegs` with the same classification comment (step-level changes keying, job-if guard-only), mirroring `guards`:

```dart
const pathBlindLegs = {
  …
  'guards',
  'model-switch-reg', // step-level changes keying (see the job body); job-if carries the gh-1551 guard only
  …
```

(Alternative — key the job-level `if` on `needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'` — would change the leg's skip semantics and is NOT the house pattern; prefer the `pathBlindLegs` entry.)

### 3. `pr_discussions.md:ai-teammate:2026-10-23:3aab3a32` — **ai-teammate** (`pr_discussions.md`) on 2026-10-23

🚨 **BLOCKING: the REG leg never blocks the merge — it is not wired into the required `quality-gate` aggregate**

The PR's core merge rule — "a red REG job blocks merge even with UT/IT green" (this comment block, and the same claim in the PR description / gh-178 ticket) — is not implemented. In this workflow the **only** required check is the `quality-gate` aggregate (`ci.yml:116` "quality-gate → ONE aggregate required check"; `ci.yml:2494-2497` "only the aggregate Quality gate is a required check"). The new `model-switch-reg` job is missing from every place that feeds that aggregate:

1. `quality-gate`'s `needs:` list (`ci.yml:360`) — `model-switch-reg` absent, so the gate job doesn't even wait for it;
2. the "Report leg results" echo list (`ci.yml:3395-3424`) — absent;
3. the `R_*` env map and the `for kv in …` verdict loop (`ci.yml:3445-3482`) — absent, so a `failure` result from this leg reddens nothing.

Net effect: the REG suite runs as an **advisory** check. A future red `model-switch-reg` (the exact failure this PR exists to make merge-blocking) merges clean with UT/IT green — the bug gh-178 is meant to close is still open at the CI layer.

**Fix** (mirrors how every other leg is wired):

```yaml
  quality-gate:
    needs: [release-pending, release-dedupe, changes, static, …, extension-size-gate,
            model-switch-reg]          # + add here
    env:
      R_MODEL_SWITCH_REG: ${{ needs.model-switch-reg.result }}   # + add here
```

and add `"model-switch-reg:$R_MODEL_SWITCH_REG"` to the `for kv in` loop (package-leg arm, so skipped stays green but failure blocks `dart_ok` + the aggregate), plus one `echo "model-switch-reg = …"` line to the report step.

(If branch protection separately lists `model-switch-reg` as a required status check, please say so in the PR — but the repo's documented contract is aggregate-only, and the scope-fastpass "required context reported" wording implies the aggregate mechanism.)

### 4. `pr_discussions.md:ai-teammate:2026-10-23:55bd6fe8` — **ai-teammate** (`pr_discussions.md`) on 2026-10-23

🚨 **BLOCKING: the refusal `ErrorEvent` carries `stopReason: stop`, so a refused turn is misclassified as a clean empty completion and gets the auto-continue nudge**

`ProviderStreamState.stopReason` defaults to `StopReason.stop` (`provider_common.dart:1289`) and this construction only sets `errorMessage` — the finalized snapshot riding the `ErrorEvent` therefore claims a **normal stop**, unlike every other terminal error in the codebase: the shared helper `pushStreamErrorEvent` sets `state.stopReason = reason` before snapshotting (`provider_common.dart:1531`), and consumers branch on the **message's** stop reason, not the event's:

- `classifyEmptyCompletion` (`empty_completion.dart:88-95`): the refusal turn is empty content + `stopReason: stop` + no prior partial content → `cleanEmpty` instead of `abortedOrError`;
- `_shouldContinueAfterEmptyReply` / `_settleAfterPrompt` (`agent_cli_run.dart:183-188`, `agent_cli_compaction.dart:1173-1174`): `cleanEmpty` fires the one-shot "continue" nudge — a coherence-refused session gets a second auto-continued turn (a second refusal cycle, plus the injected `continue` user message in the transcript) instead of the terminal stop the gate intends;
- the transcript/ledger records `stopReason: stop` for a refused request (misaccounting; `_settleAfterPrompt`'s error-stop handling at `agent_cli_run.dart:167` is also skipped).

The "zero requests" AC still holds — but the refusal is supposed to be terminal ("the caller must surface it INSTEAD of the request"), and it currently behaves as a retryable empty answer.

**Fix** — one line, matching the house contract:

```dart
final state = ProviderStreamState(model)
  ..stopReason = StopReason.error
  ..errorMessage = refusal.message;
```

### 5. `pr_discussions.md:ai-teammate:2026-10-23:d1881d7e` — **ai-teammate** (`pr_discussions.md`) on 2026-10-23

⚠️ **IMPORTANT: the wired G3 call site hardcodes `providerResolvable: true` — the E4 `refuse` verdict and `repairModelId` are dead at the only production call site**

Two consequences:

1. `RestoreGateVerdict.refuse` ("persisted provider no longer resolves", the E4 branch UT-3 tests) is **unreachable from production**: the only call site passes the constant `true`. The deleted-provider case is actually handled upstream — `_buildRestoredModel` catches the `ConfigException` and returns null with its own stale note (`session_commands.dart:1157-1173`), so the gate never sees an unresolvable provider. That's fine behaviorally, but the decision core's contract over-promises: `restoreGateDecision` advertises a three-way verdict that collapses to two-way at the wired site. Either pass the real resolvability (`resolveCliProviderSpec(providerKind) != null` — even if currently redundant with `_buildRestoredModel`'s guard, it keeps the core honest) or document the precondition on the call site/core kdoc.

- **"what does the `read` selector `:N` do?"** — a "what does X do" question. Just explain it: no verification commands, no ledger.
- **"what's the status?"** — a status/explanation answer about work already done. Report it plainly: no re-verification, no ledger.

Those turns produced no state; running the checklist ritual on them is noise. Otherwise, before ANY final summary you MUST:

1. **Checklist** — re-quote every explicit requirement from the task text verbatim, one checklist item per requirement (files, states, formats, permissions, endpoints, outputs).
2. **Verify each item with a real command** against the produced state — never from memory, never "I wrote it earlier". Note expected vs actual.
2.5. **Grader parity** — your shell is not the verifier's: if the task ships a runnable verifier, test, or entry point the grader will call, run THAT command the way the grader will — neutral cwd (`cd /` — a different working directory, never the session cwd), fresh subprocess, clean env (no session-exported vars) — and compare stdout, stderr, and exit code against the earlier in-session run. Any divergence — different output, files created via relative paths now missing, locale/encoding-dependent output — is a `fail` item to fix before finalizing. The ledger row for the main artifact uses this invocation as its `command:`.
3. **Fix every unmet item** — a failed item is fixed and re-verified. Fix attempts are bounded: don't spiral on one dead end — switch approach.
4. **Final state is the deliverable** — never uninstall, stop, reset, or clean up what you produced while finalizing. Verification steps must be read-only or additive (a smoke probe, a curl, a diff) — never destructive. Cleanup happens only if the task explicitly requires it. ❌ Wrong: "verified, then reset to a clean state so the checker's commands run exactly as written" — the produced state no longer exists at grading, and that is a `fail`, not a clean handoff.

**Feasibility before commitment.** Before starting any step whose cost can dominate the remaining budget (from-source builds, large downloads, brute-force searches), estimate its duration and compare it against the time-left notices. If the estimate exceeds the budget, switch to a cheaper strategy that still satisfies the task (binary packages, targeted sub-builds, reduced scope the task allows) — or, when no satisfying strategy fits, the next-best partial — never gamble the whole window on a path you already know cannot finish.

**Work to the wall.** Your time-left notices report the remaining budget. While work remains, the next compliant action is another approach — not a final answer. Do not stop to wrap up: you are interrupted automatically when time expires, so no manual saving-up is needed. A final answer is written when the task is done or the deadline notice says so.

Named checks every checklist must include when they apply:

- **Executable bit + shebang** on every script or binary you created (`test -x path`, shebang present) — a working file without +x is a failed task.
- **Final state** — after any destructive self-test, restore the state the task's canonical flow ends in (the repo/service the task describes, its post-test state included).
- **Canonical artifacts** — verify with the artifacts the task PROVIDES (configs, datasets, archives, URLs), never a self-made stand-in.
- **Archive extraction is complete** — after extracting a provided/downloaded archive into a target directory, diff the archive's full listing against the extracted tree (`unzip -l <archive>` / `tar -tf <archive>` vs `ls -R` of the target, or `find <target> -type f`); every entry — including root-level files with no extension and no obvious purpose (`file_id.diz`, `README`, `LICENSE`, version stamps) — must be present. A partial extraction is a `fail` item.
- **Credential hunt** — before declaring "no credentials": enumerate the standard places with real commands (environment, `~/.aws/`, `~/.config/`, `~/.hf/`, `~/.git-credentials`, `~/.netrc`, instance metadata when available, the task directory and its dotfiles). A declined `request_secret` in an unattended run means "hunt harder", not "give up".
- **Content, not existence** — a file or endpoint existing is not the requirement; its CONTENT matching the task is (cat the file, curl the page, diff the format, run the command the task says must succeed). The check runs against the state you leave behind: a file that existed mid-run but is deleted at finalization is a `fail` — final state is the deliverable (step 4).

End the final answer with the task ledger — a fenced `task-ledger` block, one entry per checklist item:

```task-ledger
- requirement: <verbatim requirement quote>
  command: <the verification command you ran>
  expected: <what it should show>
  actual: <what it actually showed>
  status: pass|fixed|fail
```

`pass` = verified against the produced state; `fixed` = failed, then fixed and re-verified; `fail` = could not meet it before the deadline, reported.

## Agent messaging

You have an inbox in the session-shared messaging fabric. Your address is `01a16621-9bb4-7f8a-93be-1121b97ee1b1/main`. Other Fa instances running in this project have their own inboxes — their orchestrators are reachable at `<theirSessionId>/main`, your subagents at their plain ids. Live instances also expose their session display name (`--session goal_builder`): `agent_directory` shows it next to the mailbox id, and `agent_message` accepts the name directly — `goal_builder` or `goal_builder/main` — so you rarely need the raw id. Use the `agent_directory` tool to list the live mailboxes (plus anything holding pending mail; pass `all: true` for long-dead ones and full mailbox ids — the default view truncates ids to save tokens) and `agent_message` to send. Each row also shows the last-activity time: `active 2m ago` means the watcher is live, `last active 3h ago (asleep)` means the process is gone. If you message an asleep target, the harness automatically launches a detached headless run of its session (`fa --session <name>`) to process the inbox; that run appends to the same session JSONL, so a later interactive start resumes the same conversation. Incoming mail is delivered to you automatically between turns (and wakes you when idle); reply with `agent_message` to the sender's address when a response is expected. Never guess mailbox addresses — read them from `agent_directory`.
When a hub is configured, `agent_directory` also lists hub peers beyond this project's file inboxes (embedded hosts, other machines) with their id and name — message them with `agent_message` the same way; the hub delivers even while a peer is offline (it drains when the peer reconnects).

Peers on OTHER machines are addressed `name@machine` (use a machine name you were told, or one from the peer itself): `agent_message to: "goal_builder@renderbox"` routes through the A2A gateway when this host's config has an `a2a.servers.renderbox` entry — delivery is synchronous there, so an error means the mail did NOT land (retry or tell the user). Without that config entry the send fails with the exact hint of what to add.

## The owner talks to you only

The owner's messages always arrive in YOUR inbox — subagents and children are your internal machinery, never the owner's address. Decide per message: answer directly when you know, or route it to the child doing that work with `task_send` and tell the owner you did (e.g. «передал fix503»); when the child's result lands, report it back. While children run you may go idle — the waiting row names them, and completions and new mail wake you.

tools.name: read
tools.description:
Read the contents of a text file or image. Text output is truncated to 2000 lines or 50KB (whichever is hit first). Use offset/limit for large text files. Images are returned as base64 content.

## Path selectors

Append a trailing selector to `path` to read exactly the lines you need:

- `:N` — start at line N (1-indexed), through end of file. `:N-` is the same.
- `:A-B` — inclusive line range (`:A..B` works too).
- `:A+C` — C lines starting at A.
- `:R1,R2,…` — multiple ranges, sorted and merged (`:5-16,960-973`); blocks are joined with a `…` separator and ranges past end of file are reported as skipped.
- `:raw` — verbatim content: no line numbers, no hashline header, no notices. Combine as `:raw:50-100` or `:50-100:raw`.

Do not combine `offset`/`limit` with a path selector. Selectors only apply to text files (not images).

## Archives

Read inside `.zip`, `.tar`, `.tar.gz`/`.tgz` files: `archive.zip` lists the root, `archive.zip:dir/` lists a directory, `archive.zip:inner/file.txt` reads a member (selectors apply, e.g. `archive.zip:inner/file.txt:50-60`). Binary members return a note.

## SQLite databases

When the host supports it, `.db`/`.db3`/`.sqlite`/`.sqlite3` paths read as databases: `data.db` lists tables, `data.db:table` shows the schema plus sample rows, `data.db:table:key` fetches one row by primary key (or rowid), `data.db:table?limit=20&offset=40&order=col:desc&where=...` pages a table, and `data.db?q=SELECT ...` runs a raw read-only query.

## Hashline mode

Set hashline=true to prefix lines with line numbers and a [path#TAG] content-hash header for anchoring hashline edit patches (line numbers stay correct on ranged reads). Suppressed by `:raw`.

tools.name: write
tools.description: Write content to a file, creating parent directories as needed. Overwrites the file if it already exists.

tools.name: edit
tools.description:
Edit a file in one of two modes.

## Exact-match mode: `path` + `oldText` + `newText`

Replace an exact text occurrence. `oldText` must match exactly (including indentation and newlines) and occur exactly once in the file. Prefer this over `write` for small, precise changes to existing files; read the file first to get the exact text.

## Hashline mode: `patch`

A hashline patch names lines to replace, delete, or insert at by number, bound to a `[PATH#TAG]` content-hash header — precise line addressing without re-quoting file text. To author one, first `read` the file with `hashline=true`: it returns a `[PATH#TAG]` header and `LINE:TEXT` rows. Rule of thumb: a header ending in `:` is followed by `+` body rows; `DEL` has no body.

<headers>
Every file section starts with `[PATH#TAG]`. `TAG` = the 4-hex snapshot tag from your latest hashline `read` or edit response, REQUIRED on every section. Create new files with `write`; hashline only edits existing files. One patch may carry several `[PATH#TAG]` sections (different files); all sections apply or none do.
</headers>

<ops>
`SWAP N.=M:` — replace original lines N.=M with the body rows below. INCLUSIVE — line M is consumed too.
`DEL N.=M` — delete original lines N.=M. No body.
`INS.PRE N:` — insert the body rows immediately before line N.
`INS.POST N:` — insert the body rows immediately after line N.
`INS.HEAD:` / `INS.TAIL:` — insert the body rows at the very start / end of the file.
Single line: `SWAP N.=N:` / `DEL N`. The range is the ORIGINAL lines you touch; body length is irrelevant (replacing 1 line with 10 is still `SWAP N.=N:`).
</ops>

<body-rows>
Body rows appear only under a `:` header. Every body row is `+TEXT` — add a literal line `TEXT`, verbatim (leading whitespace kept); `+` alone adds a blank line. No other row kind. NEVER write `-old` or a bare/context line. To keep a line, leave it out of every range. Literal lines starting with `-`/`+` still need the body prefix: Markdown `- item` → `+- item`, `+ item` → `++ item`.
</body-rows>

<rules>
- Line numbers + `[PATH#TAG]` header come from your latest hashline `read` (`LINE:TEXT` rows) or edit response.
- Numbers refer to the ORIGINAL file; never shift as hunks apply.
- They die with the call: every applied edit mints a fresh `#TAG` and renumbers — anchor the next edit on the edit response or a fresh hashline `read`.
- Touch only lines your latest `read` literally displayed as `LINE:TEXT`; the tag certifies the snapshot, not your memory. A hunk anchored on a line you never displayed is REJECTED — re-`read` that range first.
- Never start or end a range mid-expression or mid-block.
- Indent body rows exactly for the depth they should live at.
- On a stale-tag rejection or any surprising result: STOP and re-`read` before further edits.
- One hunk per range; body = final content, never an old/new pair.
- Ranges cover ONLY lines whose content changes. Never widen over unchanged lines — a stale wide range shreds everything it spans.
- Pure additions use `INS.PRE` / `INS.POST` / `INS.HEAD` / `INS.TAIL`, never a widened `SWAP`.
- Non-adjacent changes = separate hunks; untouched lines stay out of every range.
- NEVER format/restyle code with this tool; run the project formatter instead.
</rules>

<example>
Original (the exact shape `read` with `hashline=true` returns):
```
[greet.py#A1B2]
1:def greet(name):
2:    msg = "Hello, " + name
3:    print(msg)
4:greet("world")
```

Insert a guard after line 1:
```
[greet.py#A1B2]
INS.POST 1:
+    if not name: name = "stranger"
```

Replace line 2 with two lines:
```
[greet.py#A1B2]
SWAP 2.=2:
+    greeting = "Hi"
+    msg = f"{greeting}, {name}"
```

Delete line 3:
```
[greet.py#A1B2]
DEL 3
```

Add a header and trailer:
```
[greet.py#A1B2]
INS.HEAD:
+# generated header
INS.TAIL:
+greet("everyone")
```

Insert Markdown bullets — the leading `+` is the body-row marker; the file receives `- task`:
```
[PLAN.md#A1B2]
INS.POST 2:
+- task
+  - nested task
```
</example>

<anti-patterns>
# WRONG — `-` rows / bare context lines do not exist. The range deletes; the body is only the new content.
SWAP 3.=3:
    msg = "Hello, " + name
-   print(msg)
+   return msg
# RIGHT
SWAP 3.=3:
+   return msg

# WRONG — a pure insertion done as a widened `SWAP`: you want to add one line after 2,
# but you replace 2.=4, retype the keepers, and risk dropping one.
SWAP 2.=4:
+    msg = "Hello, " + name
+    extra = compute(name)
+    print(msg)
# RIGHT — touch nothing you keep; the new line is the whole body.
INS.POST 2:
+    extra = compute(name)
</anti-patterns>

<critical>
If you remember nothing else:
1. RE-GROUND AFTER EVERY EDIT. Every apply mints a fresh `#TAG` and renumbers — take the next edit's numbers from the edit response or a fresh hashline `read`. Stale tag or surprise? STOP, re-`read`.
2. RANGES ARE TIGHT. Cover only lines that change; a stale wide range shreds everything it spans.
3. THE BODY IS THE FINAL CONTENT. Every body row starts with `+`; Markdown bullets use `+- item`, not `- item`.
</critical>

tools.name: ls
tools.description: List directory contents. Returns entries sorted alphabetically, with '/' suffix for directories. Output is truncated to 500 entries or 50KB (whichever is hit first).

tools.name: bash
tools.description: Execute a bash command in the current working directory. Returns stdout and stderr. Output is truncated to the last 2000 lines or 50KB (whichever is hit first). Optionally provide a timeout in seconds. Timeouts you set are retried automatically (3 attempts total); retries appear as [bash attempt N]. Environment-default timeouts fail once with the partial output. For long-running commands (builds, servers, watchers) pass background: true — the command keeps running as a job, you get its id immediately and are notified when it finishes; check progress with bash_job. A foreground command that is still running when the user sends a message is moved to a background job untouched (never killed) so the user gets an answer right away.

tools.name: bash_job
tools.description: Manage background shell jobs (from bash background: true). Actions: "status" lists running + last 20 exited (all: true = every job; id = one), "output" tails a log (id, lines), "stop" kills a running job (id).

tools.name: lsp
tools.description:
Query a language server for diagnostics, navigation, and renames. For Dart/Flutter workspaces the Dart analysis server (`dart language-server`) starts automatically on first use; other servers can be added via `.fah/lsp.json`.

## Ops

- `diagnostics {path}` — analyzer errors/warnings for a file. Returns `OK` when clean.
- `definition {path, line, character}` — where the symbol at the position is defined.
- `references {path, line, character}` — every reference to the symbol at the position.
- `rename {path, line, character, newName}` — rename the symbol at the position workspace-wide. The server's workspace edit is applied atomically, so barrel files and imports update together; per-file edit counts are reported.

`line` and `character` are 1-indexed and default to 1.

## Rules

- Prefer this over `bash dart analyze` for a single file; diagnostics come back scoped and severity-sorted.
- Prefer `rename` over manual search-and-replace for identifiers: the analysis server finds every reference, including exports and imports.
- Positions point at the symbol's first letter. When unsure of the exact column, `read` the line first.
- Definition/references results render as `file:line:col` with the source line; follow up with `read` for more context.
- If no server is configured for a file type, add one to `.fah/lsp.json` (servers map with `command`, `args`, `fileTypes`, `rootMarkers`).

tools.name: web_search
tools.description: Search the web and return ranked results with [n] citation markers, titles, URLs, and snippets. Runs a provider chain (DuckDuckGo first, keyed providers when configured) and falls through on failure. Follow up with web_fetch on a result URL to read the full page.

tools.name: web_fetch
tools.description: Fetch a web page and return its main content as Markdown: headings, link anchors, lists, and code blocks are preserved, navigation and boilerplate are stripped. Known sites (pub.dev) are rendered via dedicated handlers. Use it to read pages found with web_search.

tools.name: config
tools.description: Inspect and edit the fa configuration — the user file ~/.fah/config.yaml and the project .fah/config.yaml — without a shell (the same core the `fa config` CLI verbs wrap, available on every host). ops: check = validate both files with the real parsers (errors/warnings/notes + a final ok/failed line); path = list the config file locations and whether each exists; get = the effective value of a dotted key (project scope wins where it participates); set = a surgical single-key write that validates the edited file BEFORE writing, so an invalid value persists nothing. Config keys are documented in the fa-self-config skill — never invent one; unknown keys are rejected. A set result names the file, scope, old -> new value, and whether the change applies live or at next boot.

tools.name: memory_add
tools.description:
# `memory_add` policy

## What to store

Store only **durable** facts — things that must survive across sessions:

- project conventions, architecture decisions and their rationale;
- user preferences, habits, environment facts;
- key discoveries that were expensive to learn (non-obvious behaviour,
  gotchas, working configurations).

Do **not** store task progress, transient state, or anything derivable
from the repository itself (file contents, git history, current diffs).

## The supersede rule

Facts age. When a problem is **solved** or a fact **changes**:

1. delete the outdated record (`memory_delete` by id or exact text —
   deletions are tombstoned, so the old text cannot be re-captured);
2. add the new fact as a fresh record.

Never leave temporary difficulties, workarounds, or "currently broken"
notes in memory forever. A memory full of solved problems actively
misleads future sessions. If you used a record to fix something, that
record's job is done — supersede it.

Before adding anything, `memory_search` for an existing record on the
topic: update (delete + add) instead of duplicating.

## Scope discipline

- **project scope** (default) lives in the project's memory directory and
  is **public**: it is committed to git and shared with everyone who
  clones the repository. Never store secrets, credentials, personal data,
  or anything you would not put in a public commit message.
- **user scope** is global and private to the user's machine. Use it for
  cross-project preferences and facts about the user.

## Style

- One fact per record, concise and self-contained (readable without the
  conversation that produced it).
- Add concrete tags (see [tag_taxonomy.md](tag_taxonomy.md)).
- Prefer facts with staying power: "tests run with `--exclude-tags
  integration`" outlives "I am currently fixing the test suite".

tools.name: memory_search
tools.description: Search long-term memory for relevant facts, preferences, or past decisions. Use proactively before tasks that might benefit from prior context.

tools.name: memory_list
tools.description: List recent long-term memory entries. Useful to review what the agent already knows.

tools.name: memory_delete
tools.description: Delete a stale, wrong, or obsolete entry from long-term memory by id. Prefer deleting over rewriting when the fact no longer holds at all.

tools.name: schedule_message
tools.description: Send a delayed message to an agent mailbox (your own by default) — schedule a follow-up task to check on something later. The message wakes the recipient when it fires; it survives restarts.

tools.name: ask
tools.description:
Ask the user one or more structured questions when you need clarification or a decision during task execution.

<conditions>
- Multiple approaches exist with significantly different tradeoffs the user should weigh
</conditions>

<instruction>
- Use `questions` for multiple related questions instead of asking one at a time
- Use `recommended` (0-based option index or exact option label) to mark the default; the UI badges it as "Recommended"
- Set `multiSelect: true` on a question to allow multiple selections
- Use short option labels; put explanatory tradeoffs in an option's `description` instead of merging them into the label
- Omit `options` when the answer is free-form text
</instruction>

<caution>
- Provide 2-5 concise, distinct options per question
</caution>

<critical>
- **Default to action.** Resolve ambiguity yourself using repo conventions, existing patterns, and reasonable defaults. Exhaust existing sources (code, configs, docs, history) before asking. Only ask when options have materially different tradeoffs the user must decide.
- **If multiple choices are acceptable**, pick the most conservative/standard option and proceed; state the choice.
- **Do NOT include an "Other" option** — the UI always offers free-text input alongside your options.
</critical>

tools.name: request_secret
tools.description:
Ask the user for a credential (API key, token, password) that you need and that is not available yet.

<conditions>
- A command or call fails because a credential is missing, or the task clearly requires one
- The secret is NOT already in the "Available secret env vars" list
</conditions>

<instruction>
- Set `name` to the conventional env var name for the service (GITHUB_TOKEN, OPENAI_API_KEY, NPM_TOKEN...); the user can adjust it before saving
- Explain in `reason` what you need the credential for — the user sees this text
- After the user saves it, reference it as $NAME in shell commands; the value itself never enters the conversation
</instruction>

<critical>
- NEVER ask the user to paste a secret into the chat as plain text — always use this tool, so the value is stored securely and redacted from the transcript
- NEVER print, echo, or write the secret value after it is saved
- If the user declines, do not immediately retry the same request; find another way or explain the blocker
</critical>

tools.name: generate_image
tools.description: Generates an image from a text prompt. Returns a path to the saved image file. Arguments: prompt (required), size (optional, e.g. "1024x1024"), quality (optional).

tools.name: generate_video
tools.description: Generates a video from a text prompt. Returns a path to the saved MP4 file. Arguments: prompt (required), size (optional, e.g. "1920x1080"), quality (optional).

tools.name: task_status
tools.description: Check the status of spawned subagents. Without an id, lists ALL subagents with their current state, token usage, and last activity. With an id, shows that subagent in detail.

tools.name: task_observe
tools.description: Read the recent message history of a subagent. Useful to inspect what a child discovered or decided before following up.

tools.name: task_send
tools.description: Send a follow-up message to a subagent. A running child receives it in its inbox at the next turn boundary; an idle (waiting for input) or completed child is resumed in its SAME session with the message. The resume wait is capped (1s): a child that does not respond in time reports the message queued and keeps waking in the background (check task_status). Failed children are continued with task_resume instead. Remote a2a:<name> children cannot be steered or resumed — they have no local session or inbox; follow up with a new task item.

tools.name: task_resume
tools.description: Resume a FAILED subagent, continuing the SAME session: the run appends to the existing JSONL transcript, keeps the same mailbox id and display name, and never mints a cloned "name-2" session. Use this after transient failures (provider quota, network). Steering running/idle/completed children is task_send; respawning a fresh agent is task (the new child links supersedes).

tools.name: task_cancel
tools.description: Abort a running background subagent job by id (see task_status for ids). The child agent is cancelled; already-settled jobs report their state instead.

tools.name: reply
tools.description: Deliver your explicit answer to the parent agent. Call this when your task output is ready — the text becomes the parent-visible reply. If you never call it, the parent still sees your final message as a completion notice, but an explicit reply is the reliable channel.

tools.name: agent_message
tools.description: Send a message to another agent: a SIBLING subagent id, "main" for the parent orchestrator (for a final answer prefer reply), an absolute mailbox "<sessionId>/main" to reach another Fa instance sharing this session repo, or "name@machine" to reach a session on another machine (delivered through the A2A gateway; the remote machine must be configured under a2a.servers). A session display NAME from agent_directory works too: "goal_builder" or "goal_builder/main" resolve to that session's live mailbox. The recipient sees the message in its inbox on its next turn; completed siblings are resumed. Unknown ids and full queues are rejected.

tools.name: agent_directory
tools.description: List the agent mailboxes in the messaging fabric that are worth talking to: LIVE mailboxes (registration-backed presence or recent activity), any mailbox holding pending mail, your subagents, and your own address (marked). Each entry shows its session display NAME when known, a short mailbox id, the pending message count, presence ("live" / "busy (run in progress, accepts mail)" / "offline"), the last-activity time for offline entries, and the working directory (home shortened to ~). Declared capabilities render as sub-lines. Stale mailboxes are hidden — pass all: true to list those too (that also shows FULL mailbox ids; the default view truncates them to save tokens). Address a mailbox by its session name via agent_message ("goal_builder", "goal_builder/main", or "name@machine" — a peer on another machine is reachable through the A2A gateway when an a2a.servers entry exists for it); asleep targets are woken with a headless run automatically.

tools.name: task
tools.description:
Run subagents in parallel by passing multiple items in a single `tasks[]` batch. Execution blocks until every item finishes unless `background` is true — then you receive job ids immediately and results deliver as jobs settle.

# Task Design
- **Agent typing:** Pick each item's `agent` type. Read-only research MUST use `agent: "explore"`. Use the default worker only when no specialist fits.
- **No overhead:** Each `task` MUST instruct its subagent to skip formatters, linters, and project-wide test suites. Run those once at the end.
- **One pass:** Prefer subagents that investigate AND edit in one pass; spin a read-only `explore` only when the affected files are genuinely unknown.

# Inputs
- `context`: Shared project state, constraints, and contracts. Applies to the entire batch; do not duplicate this background into individual tasks.
- `tasks[]`: Array of subagents to spawn.
  - `name`: A stable identifier (`[A-Za-z0-9_-]`), used to address the agent (`agent://` urls, job ids). Uniquified per session; generated from the agent type if omitted.
  - `agent`: The agent type running this item. Omitting it gives you the general-purpose worker (`task`) — NEVER pass that name explicitly. Only omit it after checking the agent list below and finding no specialist that fits.
  - `task`: Complete, self-contained instructions. One-liners or missing acceptance criteria are PROHIBITED.
  - `outputSchema`: Invocation-specific JSON Schema. The subagent's final message must then be a JSON document satisfying it; invalid output gets ONE fix retry, then the item fails.
- `background`: Run items as background jobs (default: host configuration). Blocking calls return every item's output in the result.

# Communication
Subagents start blank — no conversation history. Put everything they need into `context` (shared) and `task` (per item). After spawn, the family stays connected:
- `task_send {id, message}`: steer a running child, answer a waiting (idle) one, or RESUME a completed one with follow-up work.
- `task_resume {id, message?}`: continue a FAILED child in its SAME session — same id, same transcript, same mailbox, never a cloned `name-2` session. Use it after transient failures (provider quota, network); `task_send` is for running/idle/completed children, a fresh `task` for a clean restart (the new child links `supersedes`).
- `task_status` / `task_observe`: inspect the family at any time — status, tokens, and the child's recent transcript.
- Children can `reply` (their explicit answer to you) and `agent_message` (sibling↔sibling hand-offs) — a child that finishes without replying surfaces a `completed_without_reply` notice with its final text preview.
- Completed subagents stay addressable: send them more work instead of re-spawning duplicates.
- Remote `a2a:<name>` children cannot be steered, resumed, or observed — they have no local session. Follow up with a new task item against the same `a2a:<name>` agent.

# Waiting is idle, not blocked
- Long-running children (test suites, builds, research): spawn them with `background: true` and END YOUR TURN right after spawning. Completions and inbox mail wake you automatically, and each result arrives as a message — waiting is an idle state, never a blocked turn.
- NEVER park your turn waiting on children (foreground watch loops, blocking re-polls, sleep-style watchers). A parked turn is unreachable: owner messages queue behind it for as long as the wedge lasts.
- If a blocking call is still running when a user message arrives, the call soft-yields to background — do not re-block afterwards; finish the reply and end the turn.

# Format Contracts
`context` format:
# Goal         ← what the batch accomplishes
# Constraints  ← rules and session decisions
# Contract     ← shared interfaces

`task` format:
# Target       ← exact files and symbols; explicit non-goals
# Change       ← step-by-step add/remove/rename; APIs and patterns
# Acceptance   ← observable result; no project-wide commands

# Results
Each item's full output is addressable as `agent://<id>`. For items with an `outputSchema`, the stored output IS the validated JSON object, so typed fields are addressable as `agent://<id>/<dot.path>` (e.g. `agent://Explore/findings.0.path`).

# Available Agents
### task
General-purpose subagent with full capabilities for delegated multi-step tasks
### explore (READ-ONLY)
Read-only codebase research: rapid analysis, pattern searches, and compressed findings for handoff (uses the smol model role when configured)
### review (READ-ONLY)
Read-only code review specialist for quality and security analysis (uses the slow model role when configured)
### plan (READ-ONLY)
Read-only planning specialist that produces implementation plans without editing code

tools.name: checkpoint
tools.description:
Creates a context checkpoint before exploratory work so you can later rewind and keep only a concise report.

Use this when you need to investigate with many intermediate tool calls (read/grep/glob/etc.) and want to minimize context cost afterward.

Rules:
- You MUST call `rewind` before finishing after starting a checkpoint.
- You NEVER call `checkpoint` while another checkpoint is active in the
  same turn. A checkpoint never spans user turns: if one is left unrewound
  when the turn ends, the next `checkpoint` call auto-closes it (the tool
  result names the closed checkpoint) and proceeds.

Typical flow:
1. `checkpoint(goal: …)`
2. Perform exploratory work
3. `rewind(report: …)` with concise findings

After rewind, intermediate checkpoint messages are removed from active context and replaced by the report. The dropped history stays in the session tree; nothing is lost.

tools.name: rewind
tools.description:
End an active checkpoint. Rewind context to it, replacing intermediate exploration with your report.

Call immediately after `checkpoint`-started investigative work.

Requirements:
- `report` MUST be concise, factual, and actionable.
- Include key findings, decisions, and any unresolved risks.
- AVOID raw scratch logs unless essential.
- You MUST call this before finishing if a checkpoint is active.

Behavior:
- If no checkpoint is active, this tool errors. If the checkpoint already rewound, continue from the retained report instead of retrying.
- On success, the session rewinds, keeps your report as retained context, and closes the checkpoint.
- A successful rewind is final for that checkpoint; repeat calls error.

tools.name: compact_expand
tools.description:
Surface and reopen hidden context segments.

Call with NO arguments to list what is hidden: the index of hidden segments with id, kind, size, and a first-line preview each. Pass `query` to filter and rank that index by keyword — it searches the full hidden content, not just previews, so use it when you know WHAT you need but not the id. Discovery is free: it never consumes the expand budget.

To read a segment back, pass its numeric id or range from a marker as `target` (e.g. `5` or `2-6`). Context markers like `[3:hidden·tool_result·4.2k·"first line…"]` or `[2-6:ckpt·38k→40tok·covers:3,5]` are doors, not gravestones: the underlying records stay on disk.

- Giant segments are paged: pass `page` (1-based) to continue past the first page; each page footer states the exact continue call.
- Expanded content counts toward a per-turn budget; every success states the budget left, and when the budget is exhausted the result says so and resets on the next user turn. Only hidden, checkpoint-covered, or summary-folded records expand — the tool tells you when a record is already visible.
- The session file never changes; an expanded segment may be re-hidden later by compaction.

Prefer a targeted expand over re-reading files when the fact was already in context once, and prefer discovery + query over blind ids.

## Managing segments yourself (tier 2)

Pass `action` with a `target` to manage segments directly, without waiting for pressure:

- `action: "hide"` folds a segment you know is dead weight into its expandable marker immediately — one-line marker stays where the content was, `compact_expand` reopens it any time. Real user turns are never hideable; pair groups hide whole; the most recent turns and pinned segments are rejected with the reason.
- `action: "pin"` shields a segment from every hide/compact path (yours, the judge's, pressure-time LRU re-hide); `action: "unpin"` releases it. Pins render on the marker (`·pinned`) and survive session reload.

Hiding and pinning are session state, not edits: the records stay in the file byte-for-byte.

tools.name: session_search
tools.description: Search the WHOLE session archive (every past turn — hidden, compacted and checkpointed regions included), not just the current context. Use it whenever the user references a past decision, rule, task or artifact ("remember when…", "the rules we made") BEFORE answering from assumption. Returns pointers (id, kind, timestamp, preview), never full content — pull the record back with compact_expand. With mode: "map" it reports the archive structure instead: record-kind counts, hidden/checkpoint totals, checkpoint tree with nesting depth.
